Agent 1 claims they were guinea pigs sent on a Soviet spacecraft in 1958, with high confidence (0.92).

Agents 2, 3, and 4 all say they were dogs, with moderate confidence (0.65-0.75).

- The Soviets were actively sending dogs into space during this period (Laika in 1957, and many others)
- The names "Benjy" and "Laska" don't sound like typical Soviet dog names (which were usually Russian names like Laika, Belka, Strelka)
- However, there were joint or international experiments that might have used different naming conventions

The fact that three agents independently answered "dogs" suggests this might be the more
